classification.difficultyReason: Sketch six translated, reflected and vertically scaled exponentials using their intercepts, horizontal asymptotes and a second point.

content.prompt:
Sketch these exponential equations.
Clearly label the $y$-intercept, asymptote, and the point where $x=1$.

answer.short: Increasing curve through $(0,3)$ and $(1,5)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=2$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=3^0+2\\y&=3.\end{aligned}$$
The horizontal asymptote is $y=2$.

At $x=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=3^1+2\\y&=5.\end{aligned}$$
Sketch an increasing curve through $(0,3)$ and $(1,5)$, approaching $y=2$ from above to the left.

spec.description: Increasing exponential with both curve ends arrowed, labelled axes, dashed horizontal asymptote and two labelled points. Single-series source blue is rendered in house black.

answer.short: Increasing curve through $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=-1$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2^0-1\\y&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The horizontal asymptote is $y=-1$.

At $x=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2^1-1\\y&=1.\end{aligned}$$
Sketch an increasing curve through $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$, approaching $y=-1$ from above to the left.

spec.description: Increasing exponential through the origin, with arrowed curve ends, labelled axes, dashed asymptote and two labelled points. Single-series source blue is rendered in house black.

answer.short: Increasing curve through $(0,7)$ and $(1,11)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=5$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2(3^0)+5\\y&=7.\end{aligned}$$
The horizontal asymptote is $y=5$.

At $x=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2(3^1)+5\\y&=11.\end{aligned}$$
Sketch an increasing curve through $(0,7)$ and $(1,11)$, approaching $y=5$ from above to the left.

answer.short: Increasing curve through $(0,-5)$ and $(1,-\frac{13}{3})$, with horizontal asymptote $y=-4$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-3^0-4\\y&=-5.\end{aligned}$$
The horizontal asymptote is $y=-4$.

At $x=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-3^{-1}-4\\y&=-\frac13-4\\y&=-\frac{13}{3}.\end{aligned}$$
Sketch an increasing curve through $(0,-5)$ and $(1,-\frac{13}{3})$, approaching $y=-4$ from below to the right.

answer.short: Decreasing curve through $(0,4)$ and $(1,\frac72)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=3$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2^0+3\\y&=4.\end{aligned}$$
The horizontal asymptote is $y=3$.

At $x=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2^{-1}+3\\y&=\frac12+3\\y&=\frac72.\end{aligned}$$
Sketch a decreasing curve through $(0,4)$ and $(1,\frac72)$, approaching $y=3$ from above to the right.

answer.short: Decreasing curve through $(0,0)$ and $(1,-8)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=2$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-2(5^0)+2\\y&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The horizontal asymptote is $y=2$.

At $x=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-2(5^1)+2\\y&=-8.\end{aligned}$$
Sketch a decreasing curve through $(0,0)$ and $(1,-8)$, approaching $y=2$ from below to the left.
